checks.title: Pay may be below the minimum rate

facts.note: Uses the national minimum casual rate; your award may set a different rate.

possible_explanations: A different award or agreement may apply to this job.
There may be deductions you agreed to.
The hours you worked may differ from the roster.
Some hours may belong to a different pay period.
next_steps: Check your award rate with the Fair Work Ombudsman Pay Calculator.
Keep your rosters, clock-in records and payslips.
A union or community legal centre can help for free.
Asking about your pay cannot get your visa cancelled by your employer.

checks.title: Delivery pay may be below the minimum for engaged time

limitations: Platform exports may not include engaged time.
How the minimum is calculated should be checked against the FWC decision.

possible_explanations: The platform may count engaged time differently.
Tips or adjustments may be paid in a different week.
The minimum may differ for your vehicle type.
next_steps: Download your platform earnings and trip history for this week.
Ask the platform how this week's pay was calculated.
The Fair Work Ombudsman or a union can help you check the minimum.

checks.title: Super timing needs review

facts.note: Weekends are skipped; public holidays are not.

possible_explanations: The super fund may have taken extra days to process the payment.
The employer may use a clearing house that adds delay.
next_steps: Check the contribution date in your super fund account.
Ask your employer when the contribution was sent.
If it keeps happening, the ATO or a union can help.

checks.title: Planned shifts may take you over 48 hours in 14 days
possible_explanations: Some planned shifts may still change.
Platform online time is counted conservatively; the official method may count fewer hours.
next_steps: Adjust next week's roster so no 14-day window goes over 48 hours.
Check the Home Affairs work-hours rules for student visas.
